title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 7.67
statement: Let $V$ be the zero set of some analytic function in a strictly pseudo-convex domain $\Omega$ in $\mathbb{C}^2$. If $V$ has finite area inside $\Omega$, is it necessarily true that $V$ is the zero set of some bounded analytic function on $\Omega$? Bo Berndttson (no citation) has shown that the answer is `yes' when $\Omega$ is the ball; and easy examples show that the answer is `no' for strictly pseudo-convex domains in $\mathbb{C}$ when $n > 2$. Skoda (, ) and independently Henkin have shown (under some cohomology condition on $\Omega$) for all $n$ that $V$ is the zero set of a function of Nevanlinna class only if $V$ satisfies the Blaschke condition. (R. Zeinstra)
